text.p: Motorola Inc said Tuesday its Pan American Wireless Infrastructure Division was selected to supply approximately $35 million in digital Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) equipment to Wireless North LLC, a personal communications services (PCS) operator.
The operator plans to provide community cordless service, mobility PCS service, and cellular service to many towns and cities in Minnesota, the Dakotas, Wisconsin and Iowa.
This targeted coverage area incorporates 110,000 square miles and a has a potential customer population of more than two million.
Deployment of Wireless North's initial PCS networks is scheduled to begin by September, 1997.

Motorola said it will install its new SC604 and SC601 equipment, which are compact CDMA radio base stations. Motorola's high capacity EMX 2500 electronic mobile exchange mobile switch will also be deployed.
Wireless North is owned by several independent telephone companies.
Motorola is a leading provider of wireless communications, semiconductors and advanced electronic systems, components and services.
